Magtutulungan ang Quezon City Government at Meralco sa pagsisiguro ng isang ligtas at maaliwalas na komunidad.

Ngayong Lunes, ibinahagi ng Meralco kay Mayor Joy Belmonte ang kanilang mga proyekto at mga nakatakdang ipatupad na programa ngayong taon.

Kabilang dito ang household electrification program, at pagsasagawa ng community engagement activities, para makaiwas sa sunog at maging protektado kapag tag-ulan.

Ipinahayag naman ng lokal na pamahalaan ang mga nais nitong inisyatibo katuwang ang Meralco, kabilang ang pagtatanggal ng mga posteng nakaharang sa mga sidewalk at kalsada, electrification ng karagdagang kabahayan, at net-metering sa 50 pampublikong paaralan na lalagyan ng solar panels.

🟦 MORNING BRIEFING — JANUARY 26, 2026

⭕️ BREAKING —
• Iran reinforces across the Persian Gulf — IRGC Navy reportedly deploying additional anti-ship missile systems around the Strait of Hormuz and Hormozgan.

• Gaza: search for the last hostage — Israeli engineering units reportedly conducting a large-scale excavation at Al-Batsh Cemetery (Tuffah) for the remains of Ran Gvili.

• Mexico: gunmen opened fire at a soccer field gathering; officials tell BNO 11 killed and 12 injured.

U.S. —
• Secretary Rubio spoke with outgoing Iraqi PM al-Sudani ahead of parliament’s presidential vote, warning against a government “controlled by Iran.”

• Bombardier Challenger 650 private jet carrying 8 crashed on takeoff from Bangor International Airport (Maine); new photo released, conditions not yet reported.

• Minneapolis: anti-ICE protesters shattered windows at a downtown hotel and vandalized signage, believing agents were staying there.

ISRAEL —

• Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar, speaking in Baku, accused Tehran of a “barbaric massacre” against its own people.

• IDF says it struck Hezbollah infrastructure across Lebanon, including weapons depots and a Radwan Force-associated military building, citing violations of Israel-Lebanon understandings.

• Barcelona: over 20 Jewish graves vandalized at Les Corts cemetery; Jerusalem condemned the attack.

GAZA —
• Israeli engineering units reportedly excavating at Al-Batsh Cemetery (Tuffah, Gaza City) to recover the remains of Ran Gvili (reported as the last hostage).

IRAN —
• Forces reportedly reinforcing positions across the Gulf, especially around the Strait of Hormuz/Hormozgan; deployment claims include Fath and Moghaddam-360 anti-ship missiles and Abu Mahdi cruise missiles (image noted as archival).

• Tehran billboard footage circulated threatening the USS Abraham Lincoln.

• Parliament national security committee head Ebrahim Azizi posted an image of U.S. soldiers in body bags warning of consequences if Washington makes a “wrong move.”

• Defense cooperation with China and Russia described as longstanding and continuing “at full force.”

• State TV segment displayed Shahed drones; an officer ended the broadcast in Hebrew: “Shalom. We are very close to you.”

• Footage from the protests: demonstrator climbs a pole and smashes surveillance cameras as crowd cheers.

LEBANON —
• Qatar official says Doha will fund Lebanon with at least $420 million in grants.

• IDF reports strikes on Hezbollah infrastructure across the country (weapons depots and a military building).

SYRIA —
• Russian troops began pulling assets out of Qamishli airport in the northeast; aircraft and heavy equipment reportedly loaded onto transport planes.

• Syrian Foreign Ministry (Arab affairs head) said Damascus is committed to restoring every inch of territory and claimed no agreement has been reached with the “Israeli…” (statement continued in source).

RUSSIA / UKRAINE —
• EU approval reported for a phased shutdown of Russian gas imports: LNG fully banned by Jan 1, 2027 and pipeline gas by Sept 30, 2027.

• Medvedev: “Nukes are the most reliable way to protect sovereignty,” adding they “clear the mind” of would-be attackers.

EUROPE —
• Greece: explosion at a biscuit factory in Trikala killed 4 with additional injuries reported.

• France: Éric Zemmour argued Europe cannot wage even a small war without U.S. logistics, warning Europe has “become very weak.”

ASIA-PACIFIC —
• India: Republic Day parade featured Bactrian camels and raptor eagles; Daredevils motorcycle squad performed stunts; von der Leyen and António Costa attended as guests.

• Indonesia: major fire at Kasongan Market complex (Central Kalimantan); casualties not yet known.

• Philippines: assassination attempt targeted the mayor of Shariff Aguak (Mindanao); attempt failed and some gunmen were reportedly killed.

GLOBAL —
• Canada/China trade: Beijing says a preliminary deal with Ottawa “does not target” third parties amid U.S. tariff threats (reported).

• Niagara Falls: mist freezing into ice as polar vortex drives temperatures below −20°C.

That's your Morning Briefing. Like, comment, share and follow us.
